summary: Sara L. McClintock works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology. Educated at Columbia, CIHTS, Lausanne, and Harvard (PhD 2002 under Tom J. F. Tillemans), she has held posts at the University of Wisconsin-Madison and Emory University.
Sara Marie Conrad specializes in Tibetology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She completed an MA at Indiana University, where Elliot Sperling served on her committee.
Sarah Aoife Richardson is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. She earned her PhD from the University of Toronto by 2016 under the supervision of Jenny Purtle.

Sarah E. Fraser is a scholar of history, archaeology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies who studied at Michigan and Kobe University. She held appointments as an associate professor at Northwestern University (1996) and directrice d'études at EPHE (2000).

Sarah Harding (b. 1951) works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She studied under traditional teachers Kalu Rinpoche and Drubpön Lama Tenpa, and later held a post at Naropa University from circa 1992 to 2008.

Sarah J. Horton works in Buddhist studies, Japanology, and religious studies. She studied under Stanley Weinstein at Yale University and served as an assistant professor at Macalester College (attested 2006).

Sarah Jacoby specializes in Tibetology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Yale University and the University of Virginia, she held posts at Columbia University (2006–2009) and Northwestern University (2009).

Sarah Shaw is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. Educated at the University of Oxford under Richard Gombrich and Lance S. Cousins, she was later affiliated with Oxford's Faculty of Oriental Studies, Wolfson College, and the Oxford Centre for Buddhist Studies.
Saraju Rath is an Indologist and linguist who held posts at the International Institute for Asian Studies, attested in 2012 and 2022.

Sarasi Kumar Saraswati (1914–1980) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology who studied under Jitendra Nath Banerjea. During his career, he served as librarian at the Asiatic Society and held a post at the University of Calcutta.

Sarat Chandra Das (1849–1917) was a scholar of Tibetology and Indology. He studied civil engineering at Presidency University, Kolkata, and received instruction from Ugyen Gyatso and Sengchen Lobzang Palden Chöpel.

Sarat Sarma specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD at Manipur University, attested in 2006, where he studied under doctoral supervisor S. Shyamkishore Singh and teacher S. Lokendrajit Singh.
Saroja Bhate (b. 1942) is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. She served as a professor at Savitribai Phule Pune University, attested in 2000 and 2011.
Sarva Daman Singh is a scholar in Indology, history, and archaeology. He held posts at the University of Queensland, including Professor of History, attested in 1958 and 1987.

Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan (1888–1975) was a scholar of philosophy, Indology, and religious studies educated at MCC and Madras. He held professorships at Mysore, Calcutta, and Oxford, and served as vice chancellor of BHU and chancellor of Delhi University.

Saswati Mutsuddy specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology, having studied under Dipak Kumar Barua. She served as an assistant professor in the Department of Pali at the University of Calcutta, attested in 2011.

Satiranjan Sen worked in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Peking University, founded Cheen Bharat Sanskriti, and served as a research scholar and junior research fellow at Visva-Bharati University.

Satischandra Vidyabhusana (1870–1920) was a scholar of Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy who studied under Sarat Chandra Das and earned a PhD from the University of Calcutta. He was Principal of Sanskrit College and held posts at Presidency University.

Satoru Harada (b. 1947) works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies and earned an MA from the University of Tokyo. He held posts at the Toyo Bunko, the Eastern Institute, and as a professor at Kokushikan University.

Satoru Noriyama works in Buddhist studies and Indology and studied under Eshō Mikogami. He held teaching posts at Osaka University of Foreign Studies (attested 1995) and Ryukoku University (attested 2003 and 2013).
